item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Very well done, usually I can nitpick something but nothing comes to mind. The issue with D-class formality that I had with the last exploratory log was not an issue here, to my taste anyway, I learned that Beta-class is a thing that I'm going to look up right after I'm done yakking here, and the dynamic between the Delta (thought the D in D-class was Disposable? Read that somewhere here…), Beta, and then between them and the snakes was great; it felt like they had personalities, and a non-hostile SCP of this sort is just plain refreshing.

Also, the fate of the first Delta and the implications thereof was a neat little bundle of awesome nestled in an already excellent page.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I also agree that the "Clever girl" and such were a little too much. They'd almost work if you added some note like "[Imitating an accent] Clever girl." to make it clear that the B-class was directly referencing Muldoon. The man has probably seen Jurassic Park, so he'd probably have trouble using the phrase unironically anyway.

But I really enjoyed this log, and it made me enjoy the main SCP even more than before. I like the idea that the Foundation is now essentially containing an entire alien environment on its grounds.

I'd love to see Beta-class become more of a thing, too. The Foundation should be pragmatic before anything else, and losing valuable personnel whose skillsets don't come along every day combined with extensive and effective on-the-job training just so that you can adhere rigidly to protocol is not very pragmatic.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Alright, so it's been way too long, but I finally got around to writing another log for SCP-440. The first one dealt with the SCP-440-1 (the rocktopods), this one was the introduction to the Rock Snakes (SCP-440-2). I wanted to keep two things consistent in the piece, specifically:

- The sense that the entities in a 440-based enviroment aren't actively hostile (or friendly) to humanity. They simply exist, and reasonably act like any comparitive creature without human interference.

- D-classers not dying for any obligitory reasons. They only die if they do dumb (if understandable) things.

One of the more difficult things in the piece was the 'Beta Class' person in the story. For more information, I talked about it in this thread.

As I wrote the article, I realized it worked better if one of the 'characters' in it was a bit more knowledgeable about a 440 habitat. As I kept writing, the more the more experienced person made more sense: Jurrasic Park had its Muldoon1, after all. If a D-Class person turned out to be that sort of person, wouldn't they want to keep him around? Not staff, per se, but definately higher than D-Class.

I concede the 'Beta Class' designation is a bit clunky.

The last thing I'm a little concerned about is the amount of footnotes. I put them in so that the reader didn't have to go back to the main SCP-440 page to read about the creatures (or the earlier Log, in the case of describing dustbug colonies), but I could be convinced to remove them.

Footnotes
1. Careful eyes will notice some phrases sprinkled in from Muldoon, and/or the scene having echos of the "We Are Being Hunted" scene from the first film. Unintended, but I didn't change it.
